title: CHAI image-only histology biomarker stratifies metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer outcomes in independent trial data
summary: A computational histology AI platform built a prognostic signature from diagnostic whole-slide images in 507 CHAARTED participants and evaluated the locked signature in 684 ENZAMET participants. In the independent ENZAMET cohort, the unfavorable-risk group had worse overall survival (HR 2.6, 95% CI 2.0–3.4) and progression-free survival (HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.7–2.7); associations remained after adjustment for clinical variables. The article also reports treatment-interaction analyses, but this retrospective secondary analysis does not establish prospective treatment-selection benefit.
organization: Valar Labs and the CHAARTED/ENZAMET trial collaborators

evidence.tested: In the independent ENZAMET cohort, the unfavorable-risk group had worse overall survival (HR 2.6, 95% CI 2.0–3.4) and progression-free survival (HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.7–2.7); associations remained after adjustment for clinical variables.
evidence.unknown: The locked image-only biomarker was independently evaluated across two prospective randomized-trial datasets, but this article is a post hoc secondary analysis, not a prospective biomarker-directed treatment trial. The treatment-interaction result is suggestive and does not prove that choosing triplet therapy by this score improves outcomes. No clinical deployment or benefit claim is made. Primary journal abstract checked; no independent replication assessed.
evidence.ai_role: CHAI extracted quantitative histomorphologic features from H&E diagnostic whole-slide images and learned an image-only risk signature on CHAARTED data; the locked signature was tested in ENZAMET. Humans specified cohorts/endpoints and analyzed the trial outcomes.
